review:
SUMMARY: Three confirmed bugs in utility and type inference modules, including an off-by-one loop error, incorrect equality handling for unknown types, and missing empty-string guards.

POINTS:
- [jadx-core/src/main/java/jadx/core/utils/ImmutableList.java:63] `lastIndexOf` skips index 0 due to off-by-one error (`i > 0` instead of `i >= 0`), returning -1 for elements only at position 0 [— fix: change loop condition to `i >= 0`]
- [jadx-core/src/main/java/jadx/core/dex/visitors/typeinference/TypeCompare.java:88-89] Returns `NARROW` instead of `EQUAL` when comparing two unknown types with identical possible type counts [— fix: add `if (variantLen == 0) return EQUAL;` before the ternary]
- [jadx-core/src/main/java/jadx/core/utils/Utils.java:44,54] `cleanObjectName` and `cutObject` throw `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` on empty strings due to unchecked `charAt(0)` calls [— fix: add `if (obj.isEmpty()) return obj;` guard before `charAt(0)` in both methods]

suspicions.observation: In `lastIndexOf(Object o)`, the loop condition is `i > 0` instead of `i >= 0`. This means index 0 is never checked, so if the element exists only at position 0, `lastIndexOf` returns -1.
suspicions.suspected_bug: `lastIndexOf` skips index 0 due to off-by-one error (`i > 0` instead of `i >= 0`), returning -1 for elements that exist only at position 0.

suspicions.observation: In StringFormattedCheck.java line 88: `while ((c = str.charAt(pos2++)) >= '0' && c <= '9' && pos2 < length)` — the `pos2 < length` guard check appears AFTER `str.charAt(pos2++)`. On the second loop iteration, if `pos2` was incremented to equal `length` in the previous iteration's `charAt(pos2++)`, the short-circuit evaluation will still call `charAt(length)` before reaching the bounds check, since the assignment and charAt happen first.
suspicions.suspected_bug: IndexOutOfBoundsException when parsing format strings ending with digits after %d (e.g., "%d5" at end of string)

suspicions.observation: In Utils.java lines 43-58, both `cleanObjectName(String obj)` and `cutObject(String obj)` call `obj.charAt(0)` without first checking whether `obj` is empty. The `smaliNameToJavaName` method in the same file does check for empty input, but these two methods do not.
suspicions.suspected_bug: StringIndexOutOfBoundsException when either cleanObjectName or cutObject is called with an empty string

suspicions.observation: In TypeCompare.java line 88-89: `int variantLen = Integer.compare(first.getPossibleTypes().length, second.getPossibleTypes().length); return variantLen > 0 ? WIDER : NARROW;` — when both types have the same number of possible types (variantLen == 0), the code returns NARROW instead of EQUAL. The condition should be `variantLen >= 0 ? WIDER : NARROW` (for >= returning WIDER) or better yet, handle the == 0 case separately as EQUAL.
suspicions.suspected_bug: When comparing two unknown types with same number of possible types, TypeCompare incorrectly returns NARROW instead of EQUAL, which could cause wrong type inference results

bugs.observation: In `lastIndexOf(Object o)`, the loop condition is `i > 0` instead of `i >= 0`. This means index 0 is never checked, so if the element exists only at position 0, `lastIndexOf` returns -1.
bugs.suspected_bug: `lastIndexOf` skips index 0 due to off-by-one error (`i > 0` instead of `i >= 0`), returning -1 for elements that exist only at position 0.
bugs.evidence: ImmutableList.java:63 - `for (int i = arr.length - 1; i > 0; i--)` skips index 0; `lastIndexOf` returns -1 for elements only at position 0.

WIDER : NARROW` (for >= returning WIDER) or better yet, handle the == 0 case separately as EQUAL.

bugs.evidence: TypeCompare.java:88-89 returns NARROW when variantLen==0 (equal possibleTypes lengths) instead of EQUAL, confirmed by test showing UNKNOWN_INT vs UNKNOWN_OBJECT_NO_ARRAY yields NARROW instead of EQUAL.

Same result on /src/old. Bug is pre-existing in both trees.
